mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the principle of superposition for waves?

options.A: When two waves meet, the resulting displacement at any point is the algebraic sum of the individual displacements of the waves at that point.
options.B: The resulting displacement is always larger than the displacement of each individual wave.
options.C: Waves completely cancel each other whenever they overlap.
options.D: The principle of superposition applies only to sound waves.

mcqs.answer: When two waves meet, the resulting displacement at any point is the algebraic sum of the individual displacements of the waves at that point.
mcqs.explanation: The principle of superposition states that the net displacement of a medium due to multiple waves is the vector (algebraic) sum of the displacements caused by each wave individually. It does not guarantee larger amplitude, complete cancellation, or restriction to a particular type of wave. Options B, C, and D are common misconceptions.

mcqs.question: Two coherent waves of equal amplitude arrive at a point in phase. What is the resultant amplitude at that point?

options.A: It is twice the amplitude of each individual wave.
options.B: It is zero; the waves cancel each other.
options.C: It is the same as the amplitude of one wave.
options.D: It is half the amplitude of each wave.

mcqs.answer: It is twice the amplitude of each individual wave.
mcqs.explanation: When waves are in phase (phase difference 0°), their displacements add constructively, giving a resultant amplitude equal to the sum of the individual amplitudes. Since the amplitudes are equal, the resultant is double. Options B, C, and D describe cancellation, no change, or reduction, which are incorrect for constructive interference.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares constructive and destructive interference of two coherent waves of equal amplitude?

options.A: Constructive interference occurs when the phase difference is 0°, while destructive interference occurs when the phase difference is 180°.
options.B: Constructive interference occurs when the phase difference is 180°, while destructive interference occurs when the phase difference is 0°.
options.C: Both types of interference always produce the same resultant amplitude.
options.D: Interference type does not depend on phase difference.

mcqs.answer: Constructive interference occurs when the phase difference is 0°, while destructive interference occurs when the phase difference is 180°.
mcqs.explanation: For two coherent waves of equal amplitude, a phase difference of 0° (in phase) leads to constructive interference (maximum resultant amplitude). A phase difference of 180° (out of phase) leads to destructive interference (resultant amplitude zero). Options B, C, and D misstate the relationship between phase difference and interference type.

mcqs.question: Two coherent sources emit waves of the same wavelength λ. At a point P the path difference between the waves is λ/2. What is the phase difference between the waves at P and what type of interference occurs there?

options.A: 180° phase difference, resulting in destructive interference.
options.B: 180° phase difference, resulting in constructive interference.
options.C: 90° phase difference, resulting in destructive interference.
options.D: 0° phase difference, resulting in constructive interference.

mcqs.answer: 180° phase difference, resulting in destructive interference.
mcqs.explanation: A path difference of λ/2 corresponds to a phase difference of (2π)(λ/2)/λ = π radians, i.e., 180°. When two coherent waves are 180° out of phase, they interfere destructively, cancelling each other's displacement. Options B, C, and D either give the wrong phase difference or associate the wrong interference type.

mcqs.question: The principle of superposition for waves states that:

options.A: The net displacement at any point is the algebraic sum of the individual displacements caused by each wave.
options.B: The resultant amplitude is always greater than the amplitude of any individual wave.
options.C: Waves always cancel each other when they meet.
options.D: It applies only to transverse waves.

mcqs.answer: The net displacement at any point is the algebraic sum of the individual displacements caused by each wave.
mcqs.explanation: Superposition is a linear addition of displacements; it does not guarantee larger amplitude, complete cancellation, or restriction to a particular wave type. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: Constructive interference between two coherent waves occurs when:

options.A: The waves are in phase (phase difference 0°).
options.B: The waves are out of phase by 180°.
options.C: The amplitudes of the two waves are different.
options.D: The frequencies of the two waves are different.

mcqs.answer: The waves are in phase (phase difference 0°).
mcqs.explanation: When the phase difference is zero, the displacements add, giving a larger resultant amplitude—this is constructive interference. A 180° phase difference leads to destructive interference, while differing amplitudes or frequencies affect the pattern but do not define constructive interference.

mcqs.question: Destructive interference is characterized by:

options.A: A phase difference of 180° leading to a reduction or cancellation of the resultant amplitude.
options.B: A phase difference of 0° leading to an increase in amplitude.
options.D: Waves traveling in opposite directions only.

mcqs.answer: A phase difference of 180° leading to a reduction or cancellation of the resultant amplitude.
mcqs.explanation: Destructive interference occurs when two waves arrive out of phase by 180°, causing their displacements to oppose each other and reduce or nullify the net amplitude. Options B, C, and D describe other situations that are not the definition of destructive interference.

mcqs.question: Two identical speakers emit sound waves of the same frequency. One speaker is driven 90° out of phase relative to the other. At a point equidistant from both speakers, the sound intensity will be:

options.A: Reduced compared to a single speaker because the 90° phase difference causes partial cancellation.
options.B: Twice that of a single speaker because the waves add constructively.
options.C: Zero because the 90° phase difference leads to complete cancellation.
options.D: Exactly the same as that from a single speaker because a 90° phase difference does not affect intensity.

mcqs.answer: Reduced compared to a single speaker because the 90° phase difference causes partial cancellation.
mcqs.explanation: A 90° phase difference means the waves are neither fully in phase nor fully out of phase. Their superposition results in a resultant amplitude that is less than the sum of the individual amplitudes, leading to reduced intensity. Complete cancellation requires 180° phase difference, and full constructive addition requires 0°.
